analysis.one_liner: Adani Enterprises is the Adani Group's incubator company - it builds new, capital-intensive businesses (solar/green energy manufacturing, airports, data centers, roads, mining services, copper) to scale before they are spun out or separately funded.
tags: Q1 FY27 net loss on US settlement charge
analysis.whats_happening: Q2 FY27 (Jul-Sep 2026) results were approved just a day before this report, on 30 Oct 2026: revenue ₹38,023 crore (+74% YoY), EBITDA ₹6,316 crore (+62%), but PAT fell 55% YoY to ₹1,492 crore. This follows a messy run: a net loss of ₹221 crore in Q4 FY26 (higher depreciation from new assets like Navi Mumbai Airport and the copper plant) and a net loss of ₹1,461.5 crore in Q1 FY27, which included a one-off ₹2,644 crore charge tied to a US settlement. Separately, the US bribery case against the Adani founders was dismissed in August 2026 alongside an SEC settlement (~$18 million in fines), and SEBI settled its related-party-transaction violation case with the company the same month.
analysis.plain_terms: This isn't really one business - it's a holding company for several young, expensive-to-build businesses, so its headline profit bounces around a lot depending on which project just finished depreciating or which legal matter just got settled. The tension: the stock trades at a rich-looking P/E of roughly 66x, but that is partly because last year's profit was pushed down by one-off charges, not because the underlying business is actually earning that well - return on equity is only about 7% and return on capital about 5.3%. Revenue and EBITDA growth are genuinely strong, but that growth is coming from brand-new capacity (solar lines, airports, data centers) still ramping up, not from an already-mature, cash-generative core.
analysis.quarters: EBITDA has risen steadily each of the last three quarters - ₹4,479 crore (Q4 FY26) to ₹5,642 crore (Q1 FY27, a record then) to ₹6,316 crore (Q2 FY27) - which is the cleaner read on the underlying trend. Net profit (PAT) has been far noisier: a loss in Q4 FY26, a bigger loss in Q1 FY27 purely because of a one-off ₹2,644 crore US settlement charge (profit before that item was a positive ₹1,295 crore), and a swing back to a ₹1,492 crore profit in Q2 FY27 that is still down 55% on last year's unusually strong base. Management flagged segment strength in airports (EBITDA +55% YoY to ₹1,641 crore), new energy (solar module capacity expanded to 10GW), data centers (a new 240MW order for AdaniConneX) and copper (sales volumes up nearly sixfold). Treat quarter-to-quarter PAT swings as largely explained by one-off items and depreciation timing, not a clean signal of business momentum.
analysis.performance_read: The stock is 38% below its December 2022 peak of ₹4,157.73. That peak came just before the January 2023 Hindenburg short-seller report, which triggered the crash - this is a real market event, not a corporate-action artifact (the only listed corporate action, a 2009 stock split, is already reflected in the price history). Since then returns have been volatile and inconsistent against the Nifty: the stock is up just 2.12% over 1 year (beating a weak Nifty, down 10.92%), but up only 12.56% over 3 years versus the Nifty's 20.83%. The 5-year figure of 78.87% versus Nifty's 28.58% looks strong but is flattered by the sharp 2020-22 run-up that preceded the 2023 crash, so it overstates how smooth the ride has actually been. The stock also fell 14.29% in just the last three months, underlining how event-driven (legal, regulatory, rating news) this stock remains.
analysis.valuation_read: At a TTM P/E of roughly 66x and P/B of about 3.56x, the stock looks expensive. Why it looks this way matters: trailing twelve-month earnings are depressed by one-off items (the Q1 FY27 US settlement charge, Q4 FY26 loss from new-asset depreciation), which mechanically inflates the P/E by shrinking the denominator - this is partly a quirk of the trailing-earnings window, not necessarily the market paying up for growth. Whether it is actually cheap or expensive is a separate question: on a normalized basis, ROE of about 7% and ROCE of about 5.3% are low for a capital-intensive conglomerate carrying debt-to-equity of roughly 1.2x, so even stripping out the one-offs, current profitability doesn't obviously support the multiple.
analysis.growth_read: Revenue and EBITDA growth have both been strong and have moved together (+74%/+62% YoY in Q2 FY27, +50%/+49% in Q1 FY27), which is a healthier combination than revenue growing alone. But the growth is largely volume/capacity-led - new solar manufacturing lines, new data-center capacity, new airport infrastructure - rather than pricing power in an established business. One exception worth flagging: airports grew EBITDA (+55% YoY) much faster than revenue (+20%) while passenger traffic actually fell 6%, meaning that specific segment's recent gain was margin-led, not volume-led, and is less durable than if traffic had grown alongside it.
analysis.health_read: EBITDA is converting into reported profit inconsistently - two of the last four quarters showed a net loss, both explained by one-off charges or rising depreciation on newly commissioned assets rather than by the core operations deteriorating. Debt-to-equity of about 1.2x is moderate, and the company raised ₹15,000 crore via a QIP in July 2026 (demand 3.8x the issue size) to help fund its ongoing capex across solar, airports, data centers and copper. CARE upgraded its rating to AA/Stable in October 2026, its highest ever for the company, suggesting lenders see leverage as manageable. The bigger concern here looks like business/execution risk - running several large, simultaneous capital-intensive builds - rather than near-term financial/solvency risk. Not verified - check on Screener: absolute net debt figure and interest coverage ratio.
analysis.ownership_read: Promoters hold roughly 72-74% of the company (sources gave a range), and pledging remains low and unchanged at 0.79% - a reassuring signal given past scrutiny of Adani group pledging. FII holding has risen to about 11.65% (629 FPIs, up from 563 the prior quarter) and DII holding to about 6.72%. One point worth flagging plainly: GQG Partners, the marquee global investor whose 2023 entry into Adani stocks was widely read as a vote of confidence after the Hindenburg episode, trimmed its ADANIENT stake from 2.06% to 1.82% in the September 2026 quarter, as part of a broader roughly ₹8,000 crore reduction across its Adani group holdings. Separately, the Qatar Investment Authority is not on this specific register - its known Adani exposure is reportedly in a different group entity (Adani Electricity Mumbai), not Adani Enterprises.

analysis.one_thing: The Q3 FY27 results (expected to be reported around late January 2027, though this date is not yet officially confirmed) - whether EBITDA growth continues and PAT normalizes without further one-off charges will show whether the ~66x P/E reflects temporarily depressed earnings or genuinely thin returns on a very large and growing capital base.
analysis.data_notes: Quarterly revenue/EBITDA/PAT figures (Q4 FY26, Q1 FY27, Q2 FY27) were cross-checked across Business Standard, ScanX, Outlook Business, GuruFocus and InvestyWise and are consistent. Valuation ratios (P/E ~66x, P/B ~3.56x, ROE ~7%, ROCE ~5.3%) are from a single source as of 30 Oct 2026; other sources cited P/E anywhere from 45x to 66x depending on date/method, so treat the multiple as approximate. Shareholding data is from Trendlyne/Tijori (Sep 2026 quarter) and Angel One (GQG stake change).
